names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 12 decembrie, «Sfântul Ierarh Spiridon, Episcopul Trimitundei», with the rank word and the see left off.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 12 Δεκεμβρίου, «Άγιος Σπυρίδων ο Θαυματουργός, επίσκοπος Τριμυθούντος Κύπρου», with the rank, the by-name and the see left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 12. децембар ст. ст., „Свети Спиридон Чудотворац, епископ тримифунтски.“ — with «Свети» (“saint”), «Чудотворац» (the `wonderworker` grade §5 maps and `types` keeps) and «епископ тримифунтски» (a rank and a see) all left off, which leaves the bare forename. That is the stripping this corpus had already made on its Greek form, the bare «Σπυρίδων» read off «Άγιος Σπυρίδων ο Θαυματουργός, επίσκοπος Τριμυθούντος Κύπρου». THE FOLD THIS MAKES IS WRITTEN AND KEYED: `sr-foldpred.mjs` measured the string at one other holder, `spyridon-of-the-cave`, whose own Serbian form came off this same book for the Julian 31 October, and no READ_FOLDS key existed, so a new two-member key goes into `scripts/corpus-gate.mjs` in this commit.

birth.note: The Orthodox Church in America’s life says only "towards the end of the third century"; the bounds are that phrase, not a recorded year. The Охридски пролог за 12. децембар ст. ст. gives no year of birth either, and no age at death to reckon one from.

death.note: **Two sources on one year, one of them hedging it and one not; the display was «c. 348» before this reading and the bounds have not moved.** days.pravoslavie.ru prints the year beside his name for 12 December (old style) as «ок. 348», about 348, which is where the «c.» came from. The Охридски пролог за 12. децембар ст. ст. states it flat: „Прославивши Бога чудесима многим и користивши много, како појединцима, тако и целој Цркви Божјој, упокоји се у Господу 348. године.“ — he reposed in the Lord in 348. Two books agree on the year and only one of them calls it approximate, so the display gives the year; the basis stays traditional, neither being a document.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 12 декабря ст. ст. — «Свт. Спиридона, еп. Тримифунтского, чудотворца (ок. 348)»
Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 12 decembrie — «Sfântul Ierarh Spiridon, Episcopul Trimitundei»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 12ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιος Σπυρίδων ο Θαυματουργός, επίσκοπος Τριμυθούντος Κύπρου»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 12 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps, and the entry is the same man: the Cypriot shepherd who became bishop of Trimythous and confuted the Arians at Nicaea. **The two sources disagree about the years and the folder's `dates` are therefore left untouched.** The folder holds a birth inferred as late third century and a death in 348; saint.gr's head gives «(270 - 350)», its text «γεννήθηκε το 270 μ.Χ.» and «κοιμήθηκε στις 12 Δεκεμβρίου του 350 μ.Χ.» — a stated birth year where the folder has a range, and a death two years later than the folder's. That is for the author to rule on. The page also corrects a common statement of his birthplace, «στο τώρα κατεχόμενο χωριό Άσσια (Άσκια) της Κύπρου (και όχι στην Τριμυθούντα - σημερινή Τρεμετουσιά - όπως γράφουν πολλοί)». It prints an apolytikion, a kontakion and two megalynaria; the first two are taken and name him, the megalynaria are not kinds the schema holds. It names the towns that hold him patron and the places of his relic — incorrupt in his church on Corfu, with portions at the Alexander Nevsky Lavra and at Saint George of the Greeks in Venice — which is not drafted. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 25.12.2025 (12. децембар ст. ст.) — „Свети Спиридон Чудотворац, епископ тримифунтски.“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry, quoted whole with its closing full stop; URL year 2025. It is the fourth calendar to keep him on this menologion day, which the Russian, Romanian and Greek rows all already carry. `types` UNTOUCHED: «Чудотворац» is the `wonderworker` held, «епископ» the `bishop`, and `hierarch` was there. `dates`: the DISPLAY of the death NARROWED from «c. 348» to «348», the bounds being unchanged at 348 both ways. days.pravoslavie.ru prints «ок. 348», about 348, which is where the «c.» came from; this book states it flat — «упокоји се у Господу 348. године» — so two sources now give the one year and only one of them hedges it. `birth` UNTOUCHED: this book gives no year of birth, and the late-third-century bounds stay the `inferred` reading they were. NO `locations`: Cyprus, Trimythous, Nicaea and Corfu are four places and the folder has never held a coordinate. NO `related` ROW ADDED: `constantine-the-great` was already here, and the emperor «Констанс» this entry says he healed of a heavy sickness is no folder this corpus holds under that name — naming a Constantius or a Constans out of the emperors it does hold would be a guess. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS, where three calendars had the bishop and the wonders: that his parents were simple people, FARMERS, and that he remained simple and humble to his death; that he married in his youth and had children, and gave himself wholly to God when his wife died; that AS BISHOP HE DID NOT CHANGE HIS WAY OF LIFE, working his own cattle and tilling his own land and keeping very little of the fruit of it for himself; the list of his wonders — rain in a drought, the course of a river stopped, several dead raised, an emperor healed, angels seen and heard; and the soldier at the palace gate who took him for a beggar and struck him in the face, to whom the meek and guileless man turned the other cheek. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Soborului celui dintâi te-ai arătat apărător şi de minuni făcător, de Dumnezeu purtătorule Sfinte Spiridon, părintele nostru. Pentru aceasta cu femeia cea moartă în groapă tu ai vorbit şi şarpele în aur l-ai prefăcut. Şi când ai cântat sfintele rugăciuni, îngeri ai avut împreună cu tine slujind, preasfinţite. Slavă Celui Ce te-a preamărit pe tine; Slavă Celui Ce te-a încununat; Slavă Celui Ce lucrează prin tine tuturor tămăduiri.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Ierarh Spiridon, Episcopul Trimitundei

english.text: You were shown to be a defender of the first council and a worker of wonders, God-bearing Saint Spyridon our father. Therefore you spoke with the dead woman in her grave and turned the serpent into gold; and when you sang the holy prayers you had angels serving with you, most holy one. Glory to him who glorified you, glory to him who crowned you, glory to him who works healings for all through you.

hymns.text: Τῆς Συνόδου τῆς πρώτης ἀνεδείχθης ὑπέρμαχος, καὶ θαυματουργὸς θεοφόρε, Σπυρίδων Πατὴρ ἡμῶν· διὸ νεκρᾷ σὺ ἐν τάφῳ προσφωνεῖς, καὶ ὄφιν εἰς χρυσοῦν μετέβαλες· καὶ ἐν τῷ μέλπειν τὰς ἁγίας σου εὐχάς, Ἀγγέλους ἔσχες συλλειτουργούντάς σοι Ἱερώτατε. Δόξα τῷ σὲ δοξάσαντι Χριστῷ· δόξα τῷ σὲ στεφανώσαντι· δόξα τῷ ἐνεργοῦντι διὰ σοῦ, πᾶσιν ἰάματα.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος α’, Τοῦ λίθου σφραγισθέντος — the first hymn on the page of «Άγιος Σπυρίδων ο Θαυματουργός, επίσκοπος Τριμυθούντος Κύπρου», and it names him.

english.text: You were shown to be the champion of the First Council and a wonderworker, God-bearing Spyridon our father; and so you spoke to a dead woman in the grave and changed a serpent into gold, and while you were chanting your holy prayers you had angels concelebrating with you, most holy one. Glory to Christ who glorified you; glory to him who crowned you; glory to him who works healings for all through you.

hymns.text: Τῷ πόθῳ Χριστοῦ τρωθεὶς, Ἱερώτατε, τὸν νοῦν πτερωθείς, τῇ αἴγλῃ τοῦ Πνεύματος, πρακτικὴ θεωρία, τὴν πρᾶξιν εὗρες θεόπνευστε, θυσιαστήριον θεῖον γενόμενος, αἰτούμενος πᾶσι θείαν ἕλλαμψιν.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος β’, Τὰ ἄνω ζητῶν — on the page of «Άγιος Σπυρίδων ο Θαυματουργός, επίσκοπος Τριμυθούντος Κύπρου», printed as his.

english.text: Wounded with longing for Christ, most holy one, your mind given wings by the radiance of the Spirit, you found your action in practical contemplation, God-inspired father, and became a divine altar, asking divine illumination for all.
